passages.text: Then Jesus began to speak to them in parables: “A man planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a wine vat, and built a watchtower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people using parables.
He told them a story.
A man planted a vineyard.
He built a wall around the vineyard.
He dug a wine vat in the vineyard.
He built a watchtower in the vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to some tenants.
Then the man went away on a journey.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤρξατο αὐτοῖς ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖν Ἀμπελῶνα ἄνθρωπος ἐφύτευσεν καὶ περιέθηκεν φραγμὸν καὶ ὤρυξεν ὑπολήνιον καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν

passages.text: At harvest time, he sent a servant to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit of the vineyard.
passages.sermon:
Jesus told a parable to the people.
A man planted a vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to some tenants.
At harvest time, the man sent a servant to the tenants.
The servant went to collect some of the fruit from the vineyard for the man.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς τῷ καιρῷ δοῦλον ἵνα παρὰ τῶν γεωργῶν λάβῃ ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος

passages.text: But they seized the servant, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.
passages.sermon:
The tenants took the servant.
They beat the servant.
They sent the servant away.
The servant had nothing.
passages.original: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἔδειραν καὶ ἀπέστειλαν κενόν

passages.text: Then he sent them another servant, and they struck him over the head and treated him shamefully.
passages.sermon: The owner sent another servant to the tenants.\r\nThe tenants struck this servant on the head.\r\nThe tenants treated this servant with shame.
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ἄλλον δοῦλον κἀκεῖνον ἐκεφαλίωσαν καὶ ἠτίμασαν

passages.text: He sent still another, and this one they killed. He sent many others; some they beat and others they killed.
passages.sermon:
A man owned a vineyard.
He sent his servants to the tenants.
He sent another servant.
The tenants killed this servant.
He sent many more servants.
The tenants beat some of these servants.
The tenants killed others.
passages.original: καὶ ἄλλον ἀπέστειλεν κἀκεῖνον ἀπέκτειναν καὶ πολλοὺς ἄλλους οὓς μὲν δέροντες οὓς δὲ ἀποκτέννοντες

passages.text: Finally, having one beloved son, he sent him to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
passages.sermon:
A man owned a vineyard.
He had one son.
He loved his son very much.
The man sent his beloved son to the tenants last of all.
He said, "They will respect my son."
passages.original: Ἔτι ἕνα εἶχεν υἱὸν ἀγαπητόν ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ἔσχατον πρὸς αὐτοὺς λέγων ὅτι Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου

passages.text: But the tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’
passages.sermon:
The tenants worked in the vineyard.
They saw the son coming.
They spoke to each other.
They said, "This man is the heir."
They said, "Let us kill him."
They said, "Then the inheritance will belong to us."
passages.original: Ἐκεῖνοι δὲ οἱ γεωργοὶ πρὸς ἑαυτοὺς εἶπαν ὅτι Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτόν καὶ ἡμῶν ἔσται ἡ κληρονομία

passages.text: So they seized the son, killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
passages.sermon:
The tenants saw the son.
They seized him.
They killed him.
They threw him out of the vineyard.
passages.original: καὶ λαβόντες ἀπέκτειναν αὐτόν καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος

passages.text: What then will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and kill those tenants, and will give the vineyard to others.
passages.sermon:
The owner of the vineyard is the main subject.
He controls the vineyard.
He sees what the tenants have done.
He will come to the vineyard.
He will kill those tenants.
He will give the vineyard to other people.
passages.original: Τί οὖν ποιήσει ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀπολέσει τοὺς γεωργούς καὶ δώσει τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἄλλοις

passages.text: Have you never read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the religious leaders.
He referred to a Scripture.
He said, “Have you never read this Scripture?”
The Scripture says, “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”
passages.original: οὐδὲ τὴν γραφὴν ταύτην ἀνέγνωτε Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες Οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας

passages.text: This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”
passages.sermon: The Lord did this.\r\nThis act is marvelous.\r\nWe see it and marvel.
passages.original: Παρὰ Κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη Καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν

passages.text: At this, the leaders sought to arrest Jesus, for they knew that He had spoken this parable against them. But fearing the crowd, they left Him and went away.
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders heard Jesus speak a parable.
They understood that Jesus spoke this parable about them.
They wanted to arrest Jesus.
They feared the crowd.
They left Jesus.
They went away.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν τὸν ὄχλον ἔγνωσαν γὰρ ὅτι πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὴν παραβολὴν εἶπεν καὶ ἀφέντες αὐτὸν ἀπῆλθον

passages.text: Later, they sent some of the Pharisees and Herodians to catch Jesus in His words.
passages.sermon:
The leaders wanted to trap Jesus.
They made a plan.
They sent some Pharisees to Jesus.
They also sent some Herodians with them.
They wanted to catch Jesus in His words.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποστέλλουσιν πρὸς αὐτόν τινας τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῶν Ἡρῳδιανῶν ἵνα αὐτὸν ἀγρεύσωσιν λόγῳ

passages.text: “Teacher,” they said, “we know that You are honest and seek favor from no one. Indeed, You are impartial and teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not? Should we pay them or not?”
passages.sermon:
Some Pharisees and Herodians came to Jesus.
They spoke to Him.
They said, “Teacher, we know you are honest.
You do not seek favor from anyone.
You are impartial.
You do not look at a person’s appearance.
You teach the way of God according to the truth.
Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar or not?
Should we pay them or not?”
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθόντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Διδάσκαλε οἴδαμεν ὅτι ἀληθὴς εἶ καὶ οὐ μέλει σοι περὶ οὐδενός οὐ γὰρ βλέπεις εἰς πρόσωπον ἀνθρώπων ἀλλ’ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας τὴν ὁδὸν τοῦ Θεοῦ διδάσκεις ἔξεστιν δοῦναι κῆνσον Καίσαρι ἢ οὔ δῶμεν ἢ μὴ δῶμεν

passages.text: But Jesus saw through their hypocrisy and said, “Why are you testing Me? Bring Me a denarius to inspect.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus knew they were being hypocritical.
He spoke to them.
He said, “Why are you testing Me?”
He said, “Bring Me a denarius so I can look at it.”
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ εἰδὼς αὐτῶν τὴν ὑπόκρισιν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τί με πειράζετε φέρετέ μοι δηνάριον ἵνα ἴδω

passages.text: So they brought it, and He asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?” “Caesar’s,” they answered.
passages.sermon:
They brought the coin to Jesus.
Jesus looked at the coin.
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus asked, "Whose image is on this coin?"
Jesus also asked, "Whose inscription is on it?"
They answered Jesus.
They said, "Caesar's."
passages.original: οἱ δὲ ἤνεγκαν καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Τίνος ἡ εἰκὼν αὕτη καὶ ἡ ἐπιγραφή Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Καίσαρος

passages.text: Then Jesus told them, “Give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.” And they marveled at Him.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus said, “Give to Caesar what belongs to Caesar.
Give to God what belongs to God.”
The people marveled at Jesus.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Τὰ Καίσαρος ἀπόδοτε Καίσαρι καὶ τὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ τῷ Θεῷ Καὶ ἐξεθαύμαζον ἐπ’ αὐτῷ

passages.text: Then the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, came to Jesus and questioned Him: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man is to marry his brother’s widow and raise up offspring for him.
passages.sermon:
The Sadducees came to Jesus.
The Sadducees say there is no resurrection.
They questioned Jesus.
They said, “Teacher, Moses wrote for us a rule.
If a man’s brother dies and leaves a wife but no children, the man must marry the widow.
He must have children for his dead brother.”
passages.original: Καὶ ἔρχονται Σαδδουκαῖοι πρὸς αὐτόν οἵτινες λέγουσιν ἀνάστασιν μὴ εἶναι καὶ ἐπηρώτων αὐτὸν λέγοντες Διδάσκαλε Μωϋσῆς ἔγραψεν ἡμῖν ὅτι ἐάν τινος ἀδελφὸς ἀποθάνῃ καὶ καταλίπῃ γυναῖκα καὶ μὴ ἀφῇ τέκνον ἵνα λάβῃ ὁ ἀδελφὸς αὐτοῦ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἐξαναστήσῃ σπέρμα τῷ ἀδελφῷ αὐτοῦ

passages.text: Now there were seven brothers. The first one married and died, leaving no children.
passages.sermon:
There were seven brothers.
The first brother married a woman.
He died.
He left no children.
passages.original: ἑπτὰ ἀδελφοὶ ἦσαν καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἔλαβεν γυναῖκα καὶ ἀποθνῄσκων οὐκ ἀφῆκεν σπέρμα

passages.text: Then the second one married the widow, but he also died and left no children. And the third did likewise.
passages.sermon:
The second brother married the widow.
He died.
He left no children.
The third brother did the same.
He also married the widow.
He died.
He left no children.
passages.original: καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἔλαβεν αὐτήν καὶ ἀπέθανεν μὴ καταλιπὼν σπέρμα καὶ ὁ τρίτος ὡσαύτως

passages.text: In this way, none of the seven left any children. And last of all, the woman died.
passages.sermon: There were seven brothers.\r\nNone of the seven brothers had any children.\r\nAfter all the brothers died, the woman also died.
passages.original: καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ οὐκ ἀφῆκαν σπέρμα ἔσχατον πάντων καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἀπέθανεν

passages.text: In the resurrection, then, whose wife will she be? For all seven were married to her.”
passages.sermon:
Seven brothers each married the same woman.
Each brother died.
None of the brothers left children.
The woman also died.
People asked about the resurrection.
They asked, "Whose wife will she be in the resurrection?"
All seven brothers had her as a wife.
passages.original: ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει ὅταν ἀναστῶσιν τίνος αὐτῶν ἔσται γυνή οἱ γὰρ ἑπτὰ ἔσχον αὐτὴν γυναῖκα

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “Aren’t you mistaken, because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus addressed the Sadducees.
The Sadducees did not believe in the resurrection.
Jesus said, “You are mistaken.
You do not know the Scriptures.
You do not know the power of God.”
passages.original: Ἔφη αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐ διὰ τοῦτο πλανᾶσθε μὴ εἰδότες τὰς γραφὰς μηδὲ τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: When the dead rise, they will neither marry nor be given in marriage. Instead, they will be like the angels in heaven.
passages.sermon:
The dead will rise.
They will not marry.
No one will give them in marriage.
They will be like the angels in heaven.
passages.original: ὅταν γὰρ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναστῶσιν οὔτε γαμοῦσιν οὔτε γαμίζονται ἀλλ’ εἰσὶν ὡς ἄγγελοι ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς

passages.text: But concerning the dead rising, have you not read about the burning bush in the Book of Moses, how God told him, ‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus addressed the question of the resurrection of the dead.
He referred to the Scriptures.
He mentioned the Book of Moses.
He spoke about the passage of the burning bush.
God spoke to Moses at the burning bush.
God said to Moses, “I am the God of Abraham.”
God also said, “I am the God of Isaac.”
God also said, “I am the God of Jacob.”
Jesus reminded them of these words from God.
passages.original: Περὶ δὲ τῶν νεκρῶν ὅτι ἐγείρονται οὐκ ἀνέγνωτε ἐν τῇ βίβλῳ Μωϋσέως ἐπὶ τοῦ Βάτου πῶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Θεὸς λέγων Ἐγὼ ὁ Θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ Θεὸς Ἰακώβ

passages.text: He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. You are badly mistaken!”
passages.sermon: God is not the God of the dead.\r\nGod is the God of the living.\r\nYou are greatly mistaken.
passages.original: οὐκ ἔστιν Θεὸς νεκρῶν ἀλλὰ ζώντων πολὺ πλανᾶσθε

passages.text: Now one of the scribes had come up and heard their debate. Noticing how well Jesus had answered them, he asked Him, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”
passages.sermon:
A scribe came to Jesus.
The scribe heard Jesus and others debating.
The scribe saw that Jesus answered well.
The scribe asked Jesus a question.
He said, “Which commandment is the most important of all?”
passages.original: Καὶ προσελθὼν εἷς τῶν γραμματέων ἀκούσας αὐτῶν συζητούντων ἰδὼν ὅτι καλῶς ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτόν Ποία ἐστὶν ἐντολὴ πρώτη πάντων

passages.text: Jesus replied, “This is the most important: ‘Hear O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the scribe.
Jesus answered his question.
Jesus said, "This is the most important commandment.
Listen, Israel.
The Lord is our God.
The Lord is One."
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ὅτι Πρώτη ἐστίν Ἄκουε Ἰσραήλ Κύριος ὁ Θεὸς ἡμῶν Κύριος εἷς ἐστιν

passages.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’
passages.sermon:
God is the Lord.
God is your God.
Love God.
Love God with all your heart.
Love God with all your soul.
Love God with all your mind.
Love God with all your strength.
passages.original: καὶ ἀγαπήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ψυχῆς σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς διανοίας σου καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος σου

passages.text: The second is this: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’ No other commandment is greater than these.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He gave them a command.
He said, “This is the second commandment.
Love your neighbor as yourself.
No other commandment is greater than these.”
passages.original: δευτέρα αὕτη Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν μείζων τούτων ἄλλη ἐντολὴ οὐκ ἔστιν

passages.text: “Right, Teacher,” the scribe replied. “You have stated correctly that God is One and there is no other but Him, and to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself, which is more important than all burnt offerings and sacrifices.”
passages.sermon:
A scribe spoke to Jesus.
The scribe called Jesus “Teacher.”
The scribe said Jesus had answered well.
The scribe said Jesus spoke the truth.
God is One.
There is no other God except Him.
We must love God with all our heart.
We must love God with all our understanding.
We must love God with all our strength.
We must love our neighbor as ourselves.
Loving God and loving our neighbor is more important than all burnt offerings.
Loving God and loving our neighbor is more important than all sacrifices.
passages.original: Καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ γραμματεύς Καλῶς Διδάσκαλε ἐπ’ ἀληθείας εἶπες ὅτι εἷς ἐστιν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλος πλὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν αὐτὸν ἐξ ὅλης τῆς καρδίας καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς συνέσεως καὶ ἐξ ὅλης τῆς ἰσχύος καὶ τὸ ἀγαπᾶν τὸν πλησίον ὡς ἑαυτὸν περισσότερόν ἐστιν πάντων τῶν ὁλοκαυτωμάτων καὶ θυσιῶν

passages.text: When Jesus saw that the man had answered wisely, He said, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.” And no one dared to question Him any further.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to a scribe.
The scribe had answered wisely.
Jesus saw this.
Jesus said to the scribe, “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”
After this, no one dared to ask Jesus any more questions.
passages.original: Καὶ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἰδὼν αὐτὸν ὅτι νουνεχῶς ἀπεκρίθη εἶπεν αὐτῷ Οὐ μακρὰν εἶ ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ οὐδεὶς οὐκέτι ἐτόλμα αὐτὸν ἐπερωτῆσαι

passages.text: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, He asked, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?
passages.sermon:
Jesus was teaching in the temple courts.
Jesus spoke to the people.
Jesus asked a question.
He said, “How can the scribes say this?”
The scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἔλεγεν διδάσκων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ Πῶς λέγουσιν οἱ γραμματεῖς ὅτι ὁ Χριστὸς υἱὸς Δαυίδ ἐστιν

passages.text: Speaking by the Holy Spirit, David himself declared: ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.” ’
passages.sermon:
David was a king of Israel.
\r\nDavid spoke by the Holy Spirit.
\r\nDavid said, “The Lord said to my Lord, ‘Sit at my right hand.
\r\nStay there until I put your enemies under your feet.’”
passages.original: αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ εἶπεν ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι τῷ Ἁγίῳ Εἶπεν Κύριος τῷ Κυρίῳ μου Κάθου ἐκ δεξιῶν μου Ἕως ἂν θῶ τοὺς ἐχθρούς σου Ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν σου

passages.text: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’ So how can He be David’s son?” And the large crowd listened to Him with delight.
passages.sermon: David himself calls Him ‘Lord.’\r\nHow can He be David’s son?\r\nA large crowd listened to Jesus with delight.
passages.original: Αὐτὸς Δαυὶδ λέγει αὐτὸν Κύριον καὶ πόθεν αὐτοῦ ἐστιν υἱός Καὶ ὁ πολὺς ὄχλος ἤκουεν αὐτοῦ ἡδέως

passages.text: In His teaching Jesus also said, “Watch out for the scribes. They like to walk around in long robes, to receive greetings in the marketplaces, and to have the chief seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.
passages.sermon:
Jesus taught the people.
He warned them about the scribes.
The scribes like to walk around in long robes.
They want people to greet them in the marketplaces.
They want the best seats in the synagogues.
They want the places of honor at banquets.
passages.original: Καὶ ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν Βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῶν γραμματέων τῶν θελόντων ἐν στολαῖς περιπατεῖν καὶ ἀσπασμοὺς ἐν ταῖς ἀγοραῖς καὶ πρωτοκαθεδρίας ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς καὶ πρωτοκλισίας ἐν τοῖς δείπνοις

passages.text: They defraud widows of their houses, and for a show make lengthy prayers. These men will receive greater condemnation.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke about the scribes.
The scribes take away the houses of widows.
They pretend to be holy by making long prayers in public.
They do this only to be seen by others.
God will judge these men more strictly.
They will receive greater condemnation.
passages.original: οἱ κατεσθίοντες τὰς οἰκίας τῶν χηρῶν καὶ προφάσει μακρὰ προσευχόμενοι οὗτοι λήμψονται περισσότερον κρίμα

passages.text: As Jesus was sitting opposite the treasury, He watched the crowd putting money into it. And many rich people put in large amounts.
passages.sermon: Jesus sat down across from the treasury.\r\nHe watched the crowd put money into the treasury.\r\nMany rich people put in large amounts.
passages.original: Καὶ καθίσας κατέναντι τοῦ γαζοφυλακίου ἐθεώρει πῶς ὁ ὄχλος βάλλει χαλκὸν εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον καὶ πολλοὶ πλούσιοι ἔβαλλον πολλά

passages.text: Then one poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which amounted to a small fraction of a denarius.
passages.sermon:
A poor widow came.
She was alone.
She was very poor.
She put two small copper coins into the treasury.
These coins were worth only a small fraction of a denarius.
passages.original: καὶ ἐλθοῦσα μία χήρα πτωχὴ ἔβαλεν λεπτὰ δύο ὅ ἐστιν κοδράντης

passages.text: Jesus called His disciples to Him and said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a poor widow put money into the treasury.
Jesus called His disciples to Him.
He spoke to them.
He said, “I tell you the truth.
This poor widow has put more into the treasury than all the others.”
passages.original: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἡ χήρα αὕτη ἡ πτωχὴ πλεῖον πάντων ἔβαλεν τῶν βαλλόντων εἰς τὸ γαζοφυλάκιον

passages.text: For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.”
passages.sermon:
Many people gave money to the treasury.
They gave from their extra wealth.
A poor widow also gave money.
She gave out of her poverty.
She put in everything she had.
She gave all she had to live on.
passages.original: πάντες γὰρ ἐκ τοῦ περισσεύοντος αὐτοῖς ἔβαλον αὕτη δὲ ἐκ τῆς ὑστερήσεως αὐτῆς πάντα ὅσα εἶχεν ἔβαλεν ὅλον τὸν βίον αὐτῆς
